kept.q: Simplify sqrt(45), leaving your answer in the form k*sqrt(5).
kept.explanation: 45 = 9 × 5, so sqrt(45) = sqrt(9) × sqrt(5) = 3sqrt(5). Since 9 is a perfect square, it comes out of the root as 3.
kept.pidgin: 45 na 9 times 5, so sqrt(45) = sqrt(9) multiply sqrt(5). Since 9 na perfect square, e dey come out as 3, so answer na 3sqrt(5).

kept.q: Which of the following surds is a rational number?
kept.explanation: sqrt(121) = 11 because 121 is a perfect square (11 × 11 = 121), so it is rational. The numbers 98, 72, and 50 are not perfect squares, so their square roots stay irrational.
kept.pidgin: sqrt(121) = 11 because 121 na perfect square (11 times 11 = 121), so e be rational number. 98, 72, and 50 no be perfect square, so their square roots remain irrational.

kept.q: Given that sqrt(3) = 1.732, evaluate (2sqrt(3) + 1) / (sqrt(3) - 1), correct to 2 decimal places.
kept.explanation: Rationalize the denominator by multiplying top and bottom by (sqrt(3) + 1). This simplifies to (7 + 3sqrt(3)) / 2. Substituting sqrt(3) = 1.732 gives (7 + 5.196)/2 = 12.196/2 = 6.10.
